name: echo
plain: `echo` prints the words you give it. It is the simplest way to show a message, write a line into a file, or feed some text into another command.
Careful: bash has its own built-in echo, and the program /bin/echo behaves slightly differently. For exact control (no surprises with backslashes) prefer printf.
when: Print a message in a script.
Create a file with one line (echo hi > file).
Pipe a string into another command.

examples.title: Print text
examples.explain: Prints the words separated by single spaces.

examples.title: Keep the spaces and special characters
examples.explain: Single quotes stop the shell from changing anything inside.

examples.title: No trailing newline
examples.explain: -n leaves out the final newline. Forgetting it changes the hash. The most common hashing mistake.

examples.title: Interpret escapes
examples.explain: -e turns \n into a newline and \t into a tab. In some shells it is on by default; printf is safer.

examples.title: Show a variable
examples.explain: Double quotes let the variable expand but keep spaces safe.

examples.title: Show expanded wildcards
examples.explain: Prints the file names the shell matched: a cheap way to see what a glob does.

examples.title: Print a string in hex-escaped form
examples.explain: Prints ABC. Useful for building tiny payloads; pair with xxd to verify.

options.plain: Do not output the trailing newline.
Newline, tab, carriage return, bell, backspace, escape, backslash, hex byte, octal byte, unicode, stop output.

mistakes: Using echo -e in a script run by sh (dash): -e may be printed literally. Use printf.
Forgetting quotes around variables with spaces.
Expecting > to append: it overwrites; use >>.
Assuming echo prints the same everywhere: builtin and /bin/echo differ.
try: Hash 'test' with echo and with echo -n and compare.
Write three lines to a file with > then >>.
Use echo *.txt to see what a wildcard matches.
see_also: printf(1), cat(1), tee(1), md5sum(1), xxd(1), tr(1).
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
